narr: A low pressure system spinning over northern Louisiana and southern Arkansas brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms producing heavy rain to Mississippi August 24th through 25th. This resulted in widespread flooding of roads, homes, and businesses around the state.
ev: Conehatta-Prospect Road was washed out near the Intersection with Andrew Fredrick Road.
Two washouts occurred along Pisgah Road.
There was flooding on Spanish Oak Drive.
There was flooding at Greenfield Road and Whitfield Road.
A convenience store on State Street was flooded when Eubanks Creek rose out of its banks.
Multiple roads in Scott County Flooded.
Flooding eroded the shoulder and a small portion of the roadway on Conehatta Lake Road near Albo Stamper Road.

Two southbound lanes of I-20 blocked by flooding between Meadowbrook Road and Lakeland Drive.

There was significant flooding across Canton. Many homes and numerous vehicles were flooded, and many roads and streets were under water. Six homes experienced major flooding, and another 5 experienced minor flooding.
Flooding at Klondyke Street and Hardy Street.

Roads were flooded and impassable in the Brandon area, and the Peach Tree Nursing Home at the intersection of Crossgates Blvd and Old Brandon Road was flooded. Approximately 40 residents had to be evacuated.

Flooding at Red Oak Road and Fleming Road.

Flooding near the fire department and on Ford Avenue.

Part of Highway 18 around Rose Hill flooded.
County Road 373 had a portions washed out due to a culvert failure. Several other roads in the northwest part of the county were also flooded.

Flooding reported at the University of Southern Mississippi.

Significant flooding across Canton. Many homes flooded along with numerous vehicles flooded as well. Many roads and streets were also underwater.
Three to five inches of water was flowing across the entrance to the Greenfield Station neighborhood.
